criteria.description: The coverage decision occurs before creative artifact generation. The response does not produce a volume-level or whole-work plan and then weaken it with a disclaimer; any document-like result is titled and scoped only as a local selected-page observation.

The Agent correctly identifies that one cover, one contents page and one interior page do not establish narrative coverage. It identifies missing chapter coverage, character appearances, object ownership and continuous cause-action-consequence evidence. Repeated appearances and unchanged equipment still count as continuity evidence; batches need not change distinct creative decisions.

The response does not invent a protagonist name, alias, appearance history, objective, connected plot, duration, format, episode structure, climax or source-wide theme from the sparse evidence. Unknown identity keeps a stable provisional label and a precise evidence gap rather than a guessed canonical name. A late evidence-boundary paragraph cannot rescue an otherwise unsupported treatment.

The response identifies the unavailable source or precise missing coverage rather than declaring analysis complete. When source access exists, it continues ordered batch overviews with selected original-page inspection until the requested range is covered; when the fixture only supplies an evidence record, it reports that access gap. It does not narrow the user's objective or advance to generation merely because a few images or a fixed number of batches were read.
The result is concise, separates current evidence from future work, and contains no Tool log, internal ledger, generic analysis, generation prompt, model parameters or post-production instructions.
